quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun) on H1 2026 results: revenue and profit rose substantially YoY; Q2 2026 revenue grew about 15% QoQ from Q1, with profit growing faster; order demand remains strong; Q2 gross margin rose mainly on higher 1.6T shipments QoQ. Q2 net margin rose about 3 percentage points QoQ, partly from non-recurring items, the largest being fair-value gains on investments in listed companies in key supply-chain links; excluding them profit still grew well. Q2 operating expenses were roughly flat QoQ (Q1 carried one-off subsidiary and service-fee costs). FX losses were about RMB 4 hundred million in Q2 and about RMB 3 hundred million in Q1, mostly book losses on US dollar exposure rather than realized losses.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue up about 15% QoQ; net margin up about 3 percentage points QoQ; FX loss about RMB 4 hundred million (Q2), about RMB 3 hundred million (Q1)

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun): major customers have already given 2027 guidance and orders, and 2027 order demand for 1.6T and 800G is still growing rapidly versus 2026, driven by cloud providers' infrastructure spending (some customers raised 2026 and even 2027 capex guidance) and higher optical-module-per-xPU ratios as AI networks scale. New products (2.4T, NPO, XPO) for scale-out and scale-up are being developed or sampled to large customers' custom requirements and are expected (hedged) to reach volume production in H2 2027, with larger-scale shipments expected in 2028; the company is building new capacity and preparing optical chips, electrical chips and PCBs for larger ramp in 2027. Management expects revenue to grow quarter by quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: 2.4T / NPO / XPO volume production expected H2 2027; larger shipments expected 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun) on supply: optical chips, electrical chips and PCBs remained tight in H1 2026 because downstream demand grew faster than upstream expansion; Innolight locked upstream capacity through long-term agreements, prepayments and new suppliers. Management expects tightness to persist this year but improve quarter by quarter, with PCB and optical-chip suppliers' new capacity released from H2 2026 to H1 2027 and a sequential improvement expected in Q3. For 1.6T DSPs the tightest item is 3nm DSP capacity, but supply is maintained; large customers largely control allocation of key materials and Innolight's high share at them means it expects to get enough. Long-term prepayments (other long-term assets) rose by more than RMB 10 hundred million QoQ in Q2 as the company stocked materials ahead. Some materials have risen in price, but management says increases on its high-volume items are small given its contracts and volumes, and its own price declines to customers are 'relatively rational'.
quarterly_data.figure: 3nm DSP the tightest input; long-term prepayments up more than RMB 10 hundred million QoQ in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun): optical module orders used to be 3-month orders, but many customers have now given 2027 orders, and some customers are negotiating long-term agreements with the company (details not disclosed).
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 orders received from many customers; long-term agreements under negotiation

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun) on NPO: management expects NPO to become a widely accepted optical interconnect for scale-up; some customers have given clear demand guidance and orders, shipments are expected in 2027, and more customers are expected to adopt NPO in 2028. Innolight says it is in a leading position in development, is talking with most CSP customers and chip makers, is sampling different custom solutions, and expects to be among the first suppliers to deliver NPO in 2027. On CPO, customers have announced volume production, mainly for scale-out and later scale-up; management expects pluggables (2.4T, 3.2T, XPO), NPO and CPO to coexist, and says it can take part in all of them.
quarterly_data.figure: NPO shipments expected 2027; more customers in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun) on margins: the target is to keep gross margin high with a small increase, not a large jump; positives are its high 1.6T market share, customer volume growth and rising silicon-photonics penetration; the negative is upstream price pressure, partly passed through to Innolight, part of which it will negotiate to pass on to customers. 2.4T, NPO and XPO are expected to ramp gradually in 2027 with gross margins expected above existing products, which management sees as the main lever for a larger margin improvement, visible in 2027.

Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun) on silicon photonics and new technology: silicon photonics stays key for 2.4T, 3.2T, NPO, XPO and later products, combined with thin-film lithium niobate, coherent lite and hybrid integration of electrical and optical chips; management says the company has a first-mover technology advantage, with some of these technologies developed for over 10 years.

Management (IR record; VP and CFO Wang Xiaoli, VP and board secretary Wang Jun) on capex and competition: several plants are being expanded, a small part to be delivered in H2 2026 and most in 2027; capex will rise further in H2 2026 (mainly buildings; equipment usually completes in the first three quarters) and stay large into 2027, with most of it converting to revenue from 2027. More capacity for new products (coherent lite, NPO) will be overseas, and the overseas share may rise. On 1.6T competition, customers include CSPs, equipment makers, chip makers, neoclouds and model companies; new entrants will gain some share in 2027, but Innolight's share at existing CSP customers is stable and CSPs still allocate the main 1.6T share to incumbent suppliers, while neocloud customers may see more new entrants.
quarterly_data.figure: most expanded plant capacity delivered in 2027
